label: section_header
text: Australia ranking in the Global Innovation Index 2026

label: text
text: Australia ranks 20th among the 139 economies featured in the GII 2026.

label: text
text: The Global Innovation Index (GII) ranks world economies according to their innovation capabilities. Consisting of roughly 80 indicators, grouped into innovation inputs and outputs, the GII aims to capture the multi-dimensional facets of innovation.

label: text
text: Australia ranks 19th among the 54 Highincome group economies.

label: text
text: Australia ranks 6th among the 17 economies in South East Asia, East Asia, and Oceania.

label: text
text: The table shows the rankings of Australia over the past seven years. Data availability and changes to the GII model framework influence year-on-year comparisons of the GII rankings. The statistical confidence interval for the ranking of Australia in the GII 2026 is between ranks 18 and 21.

label: text
text: Australia has 2 clusters in the world's top innovation clusters of the Global Innovation Index.

label: text
text: Australia performs worse in innovation outputs than innovation inputs in 2026.

label: text
text: This year Australia ranks 13th in innovation inputs. This position is higher than last year.

label: text
text: Australia ranks 24th in innovation outputs. This position is higher than last year.

label: text
text: The Global Innovation Tracker 2026 shows what is the current state of innovation in Australia, how rapidly is technology being embraced and what are the resulting societal impacts.

label: text
text: Notes: Not all indicators of the Global Innovation Tracker are used to calculate the Global Innovation Index. Long-term annual growth refers to the compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over the indicated period. For each variable, a one-year growth rate is set for the short run, and ten-year CAGR is set for the long run; time windows might differ when gaps exist in data availability. The end period corresponds to the most recent available observation, which may differ among countries. Temperature change is an exception: it indicates the change in degrees Celsius with respect to the average temperature in the countries. from 1951-1980. Figures are rounded.

label: text
text: For Australia, 8 indicators have improved in the short-term and 3 indicators have worsened.

text: The bubble chart below shows the relationship between income levels (GDP per capita) and innovation performance (GII score). The trend line gives an indication of the expected innovation performance according to income level. Economies appearing above the trend line are performing better than expected and those below are performing below expectations.

label: list_item
text: The Global Innovation Index (GII) is published by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), a specialized agency of the United Nations.

label: list_item
text: Recognizing that innovation is a key driver of economic development, the GII aims to provide an innovation ranking and rich analysis referencing around 140 economies. Over the last decade, the GII has established itself as both a leading reference on innovation and a "tool for action" for economies that incorporate the GII into their innovation agendas.

label: text
text: The Index is a ranking of the innovation capabilities and results of world economies. It measures innovation based on criteria that include institutions, human capital and research infrastructure, credit, investment, linkages, the creation, absorption and diffusion of knowledge and creative outputs.

label: text
text: The GII has two sub-indices: the Innovation Input Sub-Index and the Innovation Output Sub-Index, and seven pillars, each consisting of three sub-pillars.
